subject.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should the timestamped backup migration preserve or convert existing numbered `.bak.N` recovery points, or may the new cleanup prune them on first write?
rationale: Config backups are recovery artifacts, and the current PR intentionally changes upgrade-visible cleanup behavior; accepting deletion is a maintainer product and compatibility decision, not a normal test-only choice.

options.title: Preserve or convert legacy backups
options.body: Require the PR or replacement to keep existing `.bak.N` rollback files until they are represented in the new bounded timestamp retention set.

options.title: Accept pruning on upgrade
options.body: Allow the first cleanup after merge to delete numbered backups in exchange for a timestamp-only scheme.

options.title: Defer the naming change
options.body: Keep the current numbered ring until maintainers choose a fuller config-backup migration design.

recommendation.title: Preserve or convert legacy backups
recommendation.body: Require the PR or replacement to keep existing `.bak.N` rollback files until they are represented in the new bounded timestamp retention set.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent routing signal for config backup tests and compatibility policy in this area.
